summary: Buffer-processing state machine. When the state at this+0x10 is not 204, reinitializes: calls the init function at *(this+0x17C)+0, resets the counter this+0x78 to 0 and sets the state to 204. While the active-flag byte at *(this+0x17C)+0x8 is nonzero it loops over buffered chunks: a batch boundary (counter this+0x78 at or above the limit this+0x60) flushes by calling *(this+0x17C)+4 then *(this+0x17C)+0 and resets the counter to 0; per chunk it writes the current counter and the limit into the callback object at this+0x8 (slots +4 and +8), calls the callback vtable at *(this+0x8)+0 when the object is non-null, and advances through the processing function at *(this+0x180)+4. If the counter is unchanged after a processing call it returns 0; otherwise it continues until the batch is drained. When the active flag clears, it sets the final state this+0x10 to 205 plus the nonzero-ness of the byte at this+0x41 (205 when the byte is nonzero, otherwise 206) and returns 1.

local_names.this: buffer-processing state-machine object; state at +0x10, counter at +0x78, limit at +0x60
local_names.v1: alias for &this+0x78, the counter storage read and written by the loops
local_names.v2: current counter value read from this+0x78
local_names.v3: callback object pointer loaded from this+0x8 (may be null)
local_names.v4: counter snapshot taken before the per-chunk processing call
local_names.processing_block: object at this+0x17C with init at +0, flush at +4 and active flag at +8
local_names.data_processor: object at this+0x180 whose +4 slot advances the counter per chunk

operations.description: If the state this+0x10 is not 204, take the reinitialization path.
Reinitialization: call the init function at *(this+0x17C)+0, reset the counter this+0x78 to 0, and set the state this+0x10 to 204.
If the active-flag byte at *(this+0x17C)+0x8 is nonzero, enter the batch processing loops; otherwise jump to the completion state.
First loop: read the counter v2 = this+0x78; while the counter is at or above the limit this+0x60, run a batch boundary; break out to the per-chunk loop when the counter drops below the limit.

Batch boundary: call the flush function at *(this+0x17C)+4, call the init function at *(this+0x17C)+0, and reset the counter this+0x78 to 0; when the active flag at *(this+0x17C)+0x8 is then clear, exit to the completion state.

Per-chunk loop: if the callback object at this+0x8 is non-null, write the current counter value to the object's +4 slot and the limit this+0x60 to its +8 slot, then call the callback vtable at *(this+0x8)+0.
Snapshot the counter v4 = this+0x78, call the data-processing function at *(this+0x180)+4 with arguments (this, 0, &this+0x78, 0), then re-read the counter.
If the counter this+0x78 is unchanged since the snapshot v4, return 0 (no progress).
If the re-read counter is at or above the limit this+0x60, return to the batch boundary; otherwise continue the per-chunk loop.
Completion path: set the final state this+0x10 to 205 when the byte at this+0x41 is nonzero, otherwise 206, and return 1.
Return 1 from the completion path after the final state is set, or 0 from the no-progress guard inside the per-chunk loop.
